h1: The 8 Best 1.7L Electric Kettles for Tea, Coffee and Cooking, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 electric kettles with 1.7L capacity compared on temperature control, materials, spout design and price, from under $25 up.
summary: The Cosori stainless steel kettle with temperature control is the best 1.7L model for most kitchens, since it lets you stop at the right heat for green tea or coffee. The COMFEE glass gooseneck is the pour-over specialist, the Cuisinart Electric Kettle is the premium option, and the Amazon Basics stainless kettle is the budget pick.
intro: The most common mistake with a 1.7 liter kettle is trusting the capacity number. That figure describes the brimming volume of the body, not the safe fill line, and you will usually be able to boil noticeably less than 1.7 liters without risking spills. The second mistake is assuming all of them differ only in looks, when the real differences are materials, how hot water can be set, and what the spout does.

This ranking sorts eight 1.7 liter kettles by those practical differences. We reviewed each from the spec sheet and listing, comparing wattage, material, temperature control, spout shape and price bracket. We note where a feature is not stated, and we do not invent boil times or model-specific numbers the listings do not provide.

products.name: Cosori Stainless Steel Electric Kettle with Temperature Control
products.verdict: Stainless steel body plus selectable temperature, at a price that undercuts most rivals.
products.description:
This Cosori holds 1.7 liters in a stainless steel body and adds temperature control. That feature is what separates a kettle you use for tea, coffee, oatmeal and baby formula water from one that only boils.

It ranks first because it joins steel construction to adjustable heat for a $50 to $100 price. Delicate teas are bitter when brewed with water straight off the boil, and temperature settings fix that without a thermometer. It sits above the COMFEE since steel does not break and does not show limescale as readily as glass. The tradeoff is that temperature controls add a base with electronics, so there is a bit more that can go wrong over the years.

Buy it if you drink green tea, French press or pour-over. Skip it if you only boil water for instant noodles.
pros: Temperature control suits tea and coffee
Stainless steel body will not shatter
products.idealFor: Tea and coffee drinkers who want the right temperature every time.
products.skipIf: You only ever need fully boiling water.

products.name: COMFEE' 1.7L Glass Temperature-Control Electric Kettle with 6 Preset
products.verdict: A glass gooseneck with six temperature presets for pour-over fans, at the $25 to $50 bracket.
products.description:
The COMFEE has a 1.7 liter glass body, a gooseneck spout and six temperature presets. The narrow spout controls the stream, and the presets cover the typical range from delicate tea to near-boiling for coffee.

It ranks second because the gooseneck is an actual functional advantage for pour-over, where the stream rate shapes extraction. It sits below the Cosori since glass is more fragile and shows scale readily. Thus the tradeoff here is looks and pouring precision against durability. For 1.7 liters of capacity, a gooseneck is also slow when filling a large teapot because the narrow neck limits flow.

Choose it if you make pour-over coffee or like watching the water. Skip it if you pour into big pots or cook with the kettle.
pros: Low price for a control kettle
cons: Narrow spout fills big pots slowly
products.idealFor: Pour-over coffee fans who want preset temperatures.
products.skipIf: You fill large pots or want an unbreakable body.

products.name: Cuisinart Electric Kettle
products.verdict: A 1500W, 1.7L Cuisinart for people who want a known brand and fast heating.
products.description:
The Cuisinart Electric Kettle is a 1500W, 1.7 liter model from the one of the most recognizable names in countertop appliances. The listing is sparse, but the wattage is the part that counts: 1500W is the practical ceiling on a standard 15-amp household circuit.

It ranks third because the price sits in the $100 to $200 bracket, the highest here, and you do not get temperature control or a gooseneck listed for that money. That is a poor value on paper compared with the Cosori. The tradeoff is the brand: replacement parts and customer support are easier to find, which matters if you plan to keep it for a decade.

Buy it if you prefer a name brand and plan to use the kettle daily. Skip it if you want to pay for features, not a logo.
pros: Easy to find parts and support
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a known brand for daily boiling.
products.skipIf: You want temperature settings for the money.

products.name: Cuisinart 1.7-Liter Electric Kettle
products.verdict: Plain stainless steel from a name brand, without the premium price of its sibling.
products.description:
This 1.7 liter Cuisinart is stainless steel and priced in the $50 to $100 bracket. It is a straightforward boiler with no temperature controls listed, and its appeal is the metal body and the brand behind it.

It lands fourth because it delivers a durable body for half the price of the other Cuisinart, though it adds no controls for tea. The Cosori beats it on features, and the Hamilton Beach matches it on materials. The tradeoff is that steel kettles can get hot on the outside, so keep the handle and base in mind when you pour.

Choose it if you want a solid, no-frills steel kettle from a known name. Skip it if you want presets or a see-through body.
pros: Lower price than the other Cuisinart
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a durable, plain kettle from a trusted brand.
products.skipIf: You brew delicate teas that need lower temperatures.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 1.7 Liter Electric Tea Kettle
products.verdict: A stainless steel 1.7 liter kettle in the middle of the price range.
products.description:
The Hamilton Beach is a 1.7 liter stainless steel kettle sold at a mid-range price of $50 to $100. Nothing on the page points to presets or a special spout, so treat it as a straightforward boil-and-go kettle.

It ranks fifth because it competes directly with the steel Cuisinart and offers fewer headline features. Hamilton Beach is a long-standing budget-friendly maker, and that suits people who want an uncomplicated kettle. The tradeoff is that without a feature to separate it, the decision comes down to price and look, and the Amazon Basics steel kettle offers a similar build for less.

Buy it if it is on sale and you want steel. Skip it if you want temperature control or the lowest cost.
cons: Little to separate it from cheaper steel
products.idealFor: Everyday boilers who want steel and no gadgets.

products.name: Amazon Basics Electric Stainless Steel Kettle for Tea and Coffee
products.verdict: A 1500W steel kettle at the lowest price bracket, with nothing extra.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics kettle is stainless steel with 1500W of power and 1.7 liters of capacity, priced under $25. That combination of wattage and material is the same as many costlier kettles.

It ranks sixth because it does the basic job at the lowest cost, while giving up features and the brand support of the others. The tradeoff is that budget kettles tend to economize on the lid hinge, the base contacts and the finishing, so inspect it when it arrives. It remains an easy recommendation for a dorm, an office or a second kettle.

Choose it if cost is the priority. Skip it if you want presets or long-term durability.
products.idealFor: Dorms, offices and second kitchens on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want precise temperatures or a premium finish.

products.name: Elite Gourmet 1.7L Dual-Wall Cool-Touch Tea Kettle
products.verdict: A dual-wall glass kettle that stays cooler on the outside, in the $25 to $50 bracket.
products.description:
The Elite Gourmet is a 1.7 liter kettle with a glass build and dual-wall cool-touch construction. The double wall keeps the outer surface cooler than a single-wall glass kettle, which suits households with children.

It ranks seventh because the listing mentions no temperature control, and glass kettles in the same bracket, like the COMFEE, add presets and a gooseneck. The cool-touch idea is nice, but it is not a guarantee that the lid and spout stay cool. The tradeoff is looks and a safer outer wall against fewer features.

Buy it if you have kids in the kitchen and like seeing the water. Skip it if you want temperature settings.
cons: Lid and spout can still heat up
products.idealFor: Families who want a cooler outer surface.

products.name: Cosori Electric Kettle
products.verdict: A 1.7 liter plastic-bodied Cosori in the $25 to $50 bracket, for people who want the brand cheaply.
products.description:
This Cosori is a 1.7 liter kettle with a plastic body, priced in the $25 to $50 bracket. The material is the headline: plastic keeps weight and cost down but raises questions about odor and heat handling.

It ranks last because the steel and glass models above are better choices at this price, and the plastic body is the weakest part of the design. Plastic kettles can hold a faint smell when new, so boil and discard a batch or two before drinking. The tradeoff is weight and cost against material feel.

Choose it if you want the lightest kettle for the least money. Skip it if you avoid plastic in contact with hot water.
cons: Plastic may leave a new odor
Steel and glass rivals feel better
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the lightest, cheapest Cosori.
products.skipIf: You prefer to avoid plastic with hot water.

methodology.title: Materials
methodology.description: Stainless steel, glass and plastic bodies were compared on durability, taste neutrality and how they handle heat and limescale.

methodology.title: Temperature control
methodology.description: We checked which kettles list presets or selectable temperatures, since that is what separates a tea and coffee kettle from a boiler.

methodology.title: Spout and handling
methodology.description: Gooseneck and standard spouts, cool-touch walls and capacity were weighed for pouring control and safety.

methodology.title: Power and speed
methodology.description: Stated wattage, such as 1500W, was used to compare heating potential, without inventing boil times.

methodology.title: Value by bracket
methodology.description: Features were set against the under $25, $25 to $50, $50 to $100 and $100 to $200 price brackets.

whatMatters.detail: A 1.7 liter rating is the total volume of the body, and the max-fill line sits below it. Boiling to the line leaves room so water does not spit from the spout. Check the listing for the fill marks or window, and assume you will boil a little less than the headline number.

Stainless steel is durable and does not shatter, glass lets you see scale and water level, and plastic is the lightest. Look for stainless steel on the inside of the lid and spout, since that is what touches hot water. Plastic bodies may need a boil-and-discard cycle before first use.

Delicate teas and pour-over coffee want water well below boiling, and presets fix that without a thermometer. Kettles with six presets, like the COMFEE, cover the usual range. A basic boiler is fine if you only make instant noodles, but check the listing for any selectable temperature.
A gooseneck spout narrows the stream for pour-over, while a wide spout empties faster into a pot. Gooseneck kettles are slower to fill large vessels. Match the spout to what you pour into most often.

1500W is common in this class and near the limit of a standard household circuit. Higher wattage generally heats faster, but listings seldom state boil times, so be skeptical of precise claims. Avoid running the kettle on the same circuit as other heavy appliances.

faq.q: Is a 1.7 liter kettle too large for one person?
faq.a: Not if you fill it to suit. You can boil a single mug of water in a large kettle, though most have a minimum fill line. The larger body helps if you also fill a teapot or French press.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying a kettle?
faq.a: Buying on capacity and ignoring materials. Plastic bodies may leave a smell, and glass can crack. Look at what the water touches before you pick.

faq.q: Is the Cosori worth it over the Amazon Basics?
faq.a: Yes, if you drink tea or coffee. The temperature control saves you from bitter green tea and scorched coffee. If you only boil for noodles, the Amazon Basics does the same job for less.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Rinse the interior, fill to the max line, boil once, and discard the water. Repeat if there is any odor. Place the base on a level, dry counter.
Fill with equal parts white vinegar and water, boil, and let it sit for 20 minutes before rinsing. Do this monthly in hard-water areas. Glass kettles show the scale, so you will know when to clean.

faq.q: Can I leave water in the kettle?
faq.a: It is better to empty it after use. Standing water can taste flat and leaves a mineral ring. Refill with fresh water for each boil.

finalTake: The Cosori Stainless Steel Electric Kettle with Temperature Control is the best 1.7L kettle here, pairing durable steel with presets at a fair price. The COMFEE glass gooseneck is the better pick for pour-over, and the Cuisinart Electric Kettle suits buyers who want a known brand and fast heating. For plain boiling at the lowest cost, the Amazon Basics steel kettle is enough. Choose by what you brew, not by capacity.
